title: flightdeck/compliance-fetched/v1
description: Each repository the config names, failed ones first, with what the fetch wrote for it: its newest run, the run its report came from and the commits since, or why it failed.

cut.description: Present when the output budget cut the result short, so data holds only its first rows.

budget.description: The most bytes that the run printed on standard output.

dry_run.description: Present, and true, when the run was a dry run that changed nothing.

FetchRow.description: One repository's line in what `flightdeck compliance fetch` prints.

code.description: Why the repository failed, or why its commits since are null.

commits_since.description:
Commits on the branch since the report's commit; null when not
counted.

message.description:
What gh or the file system said, for people; null when nothing
failed.

newest_run.description:
The number of the newest finished run on the branch; null when the
workflow has none or the fetch failed.

report_run.description:
The number of the run the written report came from; null when none
holds the artifact.

FetchState.description: What the fetch did for one repository.

oneOf.description: The newest run uploaded its report, which the fetch wrote.

The newest run uploaded no report. The fetch wrote an earlier run's
report when one holds it, or else removed the old report.

Nothing was written, and the repository's old files are as they
were. The one exception is a fetch whose new report is in place when
writing its record fails and moving the old report back fails too.
